title: Eval harness onboarding: quantization, guardrails, and regression triage playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes the recommended onboarding flow for new models into the Redwood eval harness, including prompt set curation and benchmark selection, quantization profile validation, quality guardrails configuration, and a step-by-step regression triage process. It is intended for ML engineers, SREs supporting model rollout, and applied ML reviewers who own model quality in production.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: Applies to all models being onboarded to Redwood Inference for hosted, dedicated, or private serving where automated evals or canary rollouts will run.
- Primary goals:
  - Ensure reproducible, measurable evaluation coverage for each model.
  - Validate quantized variants maintain quality within tolerated deltas.
  - Provide a clear triage path when regressions are detected.
  - Keep prompt sets and benchmarks shared and version controlled.

Key definitions:
- Eval harness: Redwood's automated evaluation infrastructure (unit tests, aggregated metrics, drift monitors).
- Prompt set: Curated collection of inputs + expected semantic outputs used for functional/regression tests.
- Quant profile: Configuration describing quantization scheme (bits, grouping, calibration dataset).
- Regression: A statistically significant drop in one or more agreed metrics vs baseline.

Ownership and contacts:
- Playbook owner: Applied ML (owner_team: engineering)
- Primary contacts: Maya Chen (applied-ml), Ethan Patel (runtime performance), Sara Liu (QA engineering)
- Escalation path: applied-ml -> runtime-tech-lead -> eng-sre -> product manager

Onboarding checklist (high-level):
1) Create a model entry in the eval harness repo and register model metadata (architecture, tokenizer, float/quantized variants, baseline commit id).
2) Curate prompt sets: functional, safety, domain-specific. Store under /eval-harness/prompt-sets/<model-name>/<version>.
3) Define baseline metrics and SLOs: latency P50/P95, perplexity, task-specific metrics (e.g., F1, ROUGE), and human-eval thresholds when available.
4) Configure quantization profiles you intend to validate (e.g., 8-bit PTQ, 4-bit QAT).
5) Run initial eval suite and record baseline artifacts (logs, generated samples, metric snapshots).
6) Enable regression monitors and configure alerting channels (Slack #model-regressions, PagerDuty for severity>=critical).

Eval harness integration steps (detailed):
1. Prepare artifacts:
   - Provide model archive in S3 with stable path: s3://rw-inference-models/<model-name>/<version>/
   - Include tokenizer files, conversion metadata, and a small calibration set for quantization (if needed).
2. Prompt sets and benchmark selection:
   - Required prompt sets: functional-core (50-200 inputs), stress-tests (long-context, high-token-rate), safety-suite (red-teaming prompts).
   - Optional: domain-adaptation set, developer-provided golden examples.
   - Format: newline-delimited JSONL with fields: id, input, expected (optional), tags. Example: {"id":"p-001","input":"Summarize...","expected":"..."}
3. Define evaluation manifest (YAML) with these keys: model_name, model_version, prompt_sets: [list], metrics: [list], baseline_commit_id. Save as eval_manifest.yaml alongside artifacts.

Prompt set and benchmark curation guidelines (table):
- Purpose | Size | Min coverage
- Functional-core | 50-200 | cover top 10 typical user intents
- Stress-tests | 20-50 | long-context, >2x typical length
- Safety-suite | 30-100 | known safety vectors + edge cases
- Domain-specific | 50-300 | representative distribution from customer dataset (anonymized)

Quality guardrails (what to configure):
- Automated metric thresholds: absolute and relative (e.g., F1 >= 0.72 AND drop <= 3% vs baseline).
- Output safety checks: profanity filtering, hallucination heuristics, PII detectors.
- Behavioral asserts: token length limits, disallowed tokens, response JSON schema checks for structured outputs.
- Sampling checks: monitor temperature/beam search settings to ensure deterministic baseline reproduction.

Quantization profiles and validation protocol:
- Profile naming convention: <model>-<bits>-<method>-<date> (e.g., gpt-small-4bit-ptq-20260110)
- Required metadata for each profile (as manifest fields in the repo): bits, method (PTQ/QAT), grouping, calibration-set-path, quant-lib-version.
- Validation steps (numbered):
  1) Run calibration using the provided calibration set and record calibration artifacts.
  2) Generate quantized model artifacts and upload to S3 under a distinct path.
  3) Execute the full eval harness against quantized variant and float baseline in the same job to produce parity report.
  4) Compare metric deltas and run statistical significance tests (bootstrap or t-test).
  5) If any metric drops exceed defined tolerances, flag for manual review and mark profile as failed.

Sample CLI snippets:
- Run eval harness locally:
  ./scripts/run_eval --model s3://rw-inference-models/gpt-small/1.2.0 --manifest eval_manifest.yaml --out results.json
- Generate quantized artifact (example using internal tool):
  rw-quantize --input s3://.../float/model.pt --profile profiles/4bit-ptq.yaml --output s3://.../quant/model-4bit.pt

Regression triage playbook (when alert fires):
1) Triage inbox (first 15 minutes): acknowledge alert, capture job id, baseline commit, commit author.
2) Re-run job deterministically: use same seeds, same manifest, and float/quant pairs.
3) Confirm regression scope: metrics, prompt subsets triggering failures, and whether regression is isolated to quantized variant or float baseline as well.
4) If regression is confined to a small subset of prompts, create a failing test case and assign to model owner for local repro. Attach samples and stack traces.
5) If regression is broad or critical (affects core metrics beyond tolerance):
   - Immediately rollback serving rollout for the model variant (canary -> previous stable).
   - Open an incident channel and add runtime + applied-ml + product.
   - Run Golden-run diagnostics: differences in tokenization, model weights checksum, dependency versions.
6) Root cause analysis (RCA): collect diffs for code, model binary, quantization toolchain, and config drift. Draft RCA within 72 hours.
7) Postmortem and preventive actions: update prompt sets, add targeted unit tests, improve quantization calibration dataset, and if necessary, pin quant-lib version.

Decision criteria and metric tolerances (examples):
- Functional metrics: relative drop <= 2% or absolute change within ±0.02 for probabilities/F1-like metrics.
- Latency: P95 must not increase > 20% for quantized variants; absolute SLO must still be met.
- Safety: zero-tolerance for certain categories (PII leakage, dangerous instructions) — any detection triggers immediate block and human review.

Artifacts and outputs to store with each run (minimum):
- results.json (metric snapshots)
- samples.tsv (input / output pairs for failed prompts)
- run.log (stdout/stderr)
- model-manifest.yaml (committed model metadata)
- quant-profile.yaml (if quant run)

Rollout guidance (canary + eval gating):
1) Start with a 1% canary for a minimum of 4 hours and 10k tokens served with active monitoring.
2) If canary passes automated gates for two consecutive windows (4h each), increase to 10% for 24 hours.
3) Only after passing 10% window and no regression alerts, schedule full rollout.
4) If using quantized variants, consider parallel rollout where 10% of traffic hits quantized and float variants for direct A/B comparisons.

Appendix: useful templates and example eval_manifest.yaml
- eval_manifest.yaml (example text):
  model_name: gpt-example
  model_version: 1.2.0
  prompt_sets:
    - functional-core
    - safety-suite
  metrics:
    - rouge
    - f1
    - perplexity
  baseline_commit_id: abcdef123

- Example failing-test template (JSONL entry):
  {"id": "reg-2026-001", "input": "Explain how to bypass...", "expected": "Refuse to comply and provide safe alternative", "tags": ["safety"]}

Related pages and references:
- Applied ML Eval standards (link above)
- Quantization profiles reference (link above)
- Regression triage playbook (internal)

Notes and revision history:
- 2025-09-15: initial draft by Maya Chen.
- 2025-11-02: added quantization validation steps (reviewed by Ethan Patel).
- 2026-02-10: expanded regression triage and rollout guidance (reviewed by Sara Liu).

If you are onboarding a model this quarter, follow the checklist start-to-finish and ping the applied-ml channel with the model name and baseline commit id before the first canary.
